note: Generated by tools/assets/process_materials.py from tools/assets/materials-map.json. Do not edit.
uv: World-scale UVs: 1 UV unit = 1 metre on the surface. Walls: u = metres along the wall (to the right when facing it), v = metres up from the floor. Floors and ceilings: u = x, v = z in the house's local frame. Roofs: u along the eaves, v up the slope. The library divides by each material's 'scale' (metres per tile, [u, v]) and flips v so pictures read upright; 'rotate' (degrees) turns the pattern on the surface (floorboards across a room, vertical boards on a wall). Props keep their own glTF UVs (scale 1).

boardbatten.use: vertical boards with battens; paint colours tint it

brass.use: old brass hardware: polished, scratched, tarnished in patches; a tint makes brass or bronze

bricks089.use: random-coursed grey stone (foundations, chapel, cemetery wall)

carpet013n.use: wool carpet, graded neutral so colours tint it

cedarshakes.use: split cedar shakes, graded light so colours tint them (roofs, shingle siding)

fishscale.use: painted fish-scale shingles, graded light so paint tints them

paintedwood.use: enamel paint on wood, brushed along the piece (trim, wainscot, doors); paint colours tint it

roofingtiles003.use: rectangular slate; asphalt shingles by tint

stainedwood.use: flat-sawn wood under varnish, two boards across, graded light so a stain tints it

standingseam.use: standing-seam metal roof, one rib per tile

woodsiding005.use: dark stained boards; 1970s panelling when turned upright

woodsiding009n.use: painted clapboard, graded neutral so paint colours tint it
